articles.title: In the early 1900s, prickly pear spread over 20 million hectares in Queensland, threatening ecosystems with its rapid growth of 1,000 hectares daily
articles.description: An introduced cactus became an environmental disaster across Australia's landscapes. Governments tried many measures, but nothing effectively stopped the prickly pear's spread. Scientists then introduced a South American moth, Cactoblastis cactorum, as a biological control agent. This moth's larvae destroyed the invasive cactus, returning millions of hectares of land. The prickly pear case remains a landmark example of successful biological weed management.

articles.title: On cam: startling health update on Sonam Wangchuk given by doctor on day 19 of hunger strike| CJP
articles.description: Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk has completed the 19th day of his indefinite hunger strike, with doctors confirming that he has now lost more than 9 kilograms. According to Dr. Satish Lamba, Wangchuk's current weight is 56.9 kg, while his blood sugar, pulse and blood pressure remain under close medical observation. Doctors said Wangchuk is currently in the second stage of prolonged fasting, marked by elevated uric acid levels due to muscle breakdown. They warned that a possible third stage, involving organ-related complications, could emerge, prompting round-the-clock monitoring and a "wait and watch" approach. Watch the latest update on Sonam Wangchuk's health and the medical team's assessment.
